findings.title: Login-cache invalidation can be skipped when the original IDP is resolved through an organization-aware wrapper
findings.body: In update(), the original model is loaded with getById(), which returns an organization-aware IdentityProviderModel whose isEnabled() is false when the linked organization is disabled. registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() then applies LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate() to this wrapped original. If the organization is disabled, an update that removes login eligibility (for example hideOnLogin=true, linkOnly=true, or broker.public=false) can be evaluated as false -> false and no login-cache invalidation is registered. When the organization is later enabled, the stale getForLogin cache can still contain the provider, and callers that only re-check isEnabled() may display a hidden, private, or link-only provider. Use the raw delegate model for the original state, or invalidate whenever login-related fields change.

findings.title: getForLogin cache does not react to organization invalidation
findings.body: getForLogin() checks only isInvalid(cacheKey), where cacheKey is realm+FetchMode. It stores organization-specific result sets inside that mode-level cache entry using organizationId as a search key, but it does not check organization invalidation or otherwise tie the entry to organization lifecycle changes. getByOrganization() at least checks isInvalid(orgId). As a result, organization changes such as enable/disable or update do not refresh these cached login lists, so stale organization-scoped IDP lists can be returned until an unrelated IDP change invalidates the mode key.

findings.title: Cached getForLogin results are returned without re-validating login eligibility
findings.body: In the cached path, getForLogin() resolves each cached internal ID and adds the model to the result without verifying that it still satisfies the login criteria (enabled, not link-only, not hidden, and public when organization-linked). The correctness of the cache therefore depends entirely on invalidations being complete. If an invalidation is missed, for example when an IDP is updated while its organization is disabled, this method can return providers that should no longer be available for login. Filtering cached entries before returning them would prevent stale ineligible providers from being exposed.

findings.title: Test cleanup registers removal of the wrong alias
findings.body: testCacheIDPForLogin creates providers with aliases idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-19 and later idp-alias-20, but registers cleanup for the literal alias instead of the generated alias. The created providers are therefore not removed, leaving test data behind and potentially affecting other tests. The same problem occurs at line 425. Cleanup should use the actual provider alias.

findings.title: Mode-level login cache can accumulate unbounded organization search keys
findings.body: cacheKeyForLogin() is keyed only by realm and FetchMode, while each distinct organizationId queried is stored as another search key inside the same IdentityProviderListQuery. There is no eviction of individual organization search keys; adding a new one invalidates and replaces the whole entry. In realms with many organizations this cached object can grow large and cause extra invalidation/replication overhead. Consider keying by organization or limiting/evicting search keys.

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException in remove() for a nonexistent alias
findings.body: remove() fetches storedIdp from the delegate before deletion. If the alias does not exist and isInvalid(cacheKey) is true, storedIdp is null and registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) dereferences it, causing a NullPointerException. This can turn removal of a nonexistent alias into an internal error in some cache states. Guard against a null storedIdp before registering invalidation.
